tasks.prompt:
Task: Interval groups with index provenance.
Create solution.py containing def solve(payload, config). payload is an arbitrary-order list of intervals with integer start/end and start < end; each denotes [start,end). config gap is a nonnegative integer. Sort conceptually by (start,end,original index). Start a group from the first interval. A following interval joins the current group if its start <= the current group maximum end + gap; joining updates the maximum end. Otherwise start a new group. Thus touching intervals DO join at gap0 despite half-open notation, and equality with the gap boundary joins. This is transitive grouping, not comparing only with the immediately previous interval end. Return {groups}, where groups is the list of {start,end,indices} in increasing group start order. start/end are the minimum start and maximum end of all original intervals in that group; indices are original zero-based payload positions sorted numerically within each group. Duplicate intervals keep their distinct indices. Empty input returns {groups:[]}. Use exact integer arithmetic, permit negative endpoints, and do not mutate payload or config.
The project contains config.json with the configuration and one sample INPUT (no expected output). You must first make exactly one read tool call for path config.json, with whole=true and raw=true, and consume its result. Then make exactly one write tool call for path solution.py containing your complete implementation. These are the only allowed tools and paths. Do not call bash, list, edit, more, web, search, or any other tool. Do not read solution.py or any other file. No second write or correction is permitted. After the write, finish with a brief plain answer. External tests will run once after your first attempt; do not try to run them.

Task: Deterministic dependency layers.
Create solution.py containing def solve(payload, config). payload is an arbitrary-order list of task records {id,deps}. id values are unique strings, including possible empty/Unicode strings; deps is a list of exact string IDs and may contain duplicates, self-dependencies, cycles, or IDs absent from payload. config order is either input or lex. Start with no completed tasks. In EACH round select ALL remaining tasks whose every dependency was completed in an EARLIER round. Emit their IDs as one layer, then mark the entire layer complete. Never unlock another task within the same round. With order=input, list IDs in original payload order within each layer; with order=lex, use Python string ascending order. Stop when no tasks are ready. Return {layers,unresolved}; unresolved contains all remaining task IDs in the configured order. An absent dependency is never completed, so it blocks its task and dependents; cycles/self-dependencies also remain unresolved. Duplicate dependencies impose no extra work. Empty payload returns {layers:[],unresolved:[]}. Compare IDs exactly without normalization, and do not mutate payload or config.
